subject: Post-demo: HealthSync geo SLO / performance qualification and next steps
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara@healthsync.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: quick SLO follow-up and data residency check

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and a list of items we need to qualify so we can size a proposal that preserves your latency targets and data residency constraints.

Key performance context from demo (confirm or correct):
- Target p95 generation latency: US <= 120–150 ms (interactive UI), EU <= 180–220 ms, APAC <= 250–350 ms (tolerance for warm-up).
- Peak throughput estimate: 600–1,200 RPS across the org during daily spikes; baseline ~120 RPS.
- Concurrent sessions (long-lived streaming chat): ~180 concurrent streams at peak; average idle TTL ~2 minutes.
- Typical prompt/response token lengths: 40 tokens in, 120 tokens out (avg); bursts up to 1,000 tokens for batch exports.
- Data residency: EU customers' PII must remain in EU regions; logs and KV cache for EU tenants must be EU-only.

Questions / items we need from HealthSync to finalize qualification:
1) Can you confirm peak RPS per region (US/EU/APAC) and the weekday/timezone pattern (we can map autoscaling windows accordingly)?
2) For the streaming use case: do you expect single-shard streams or cross-region fan-out (i.e., a single user session read/written from multiple regions)?
3) Are there any strict cold-start SLAs (e.g., first-token latency requirements after an idle window)?
4) Any compliance evidence required beyond SOC2 (e.g., data residency attestation language, HIPAA BAA comments)?

Attachments: I’ve attached a short matrix template (healthsync_slo_requirements.xlsx) you can fill with per-region numbers.

Next steps I propose:
- You populate the sheet with region-level peak RPS and concurrency by EOD Thu (May 13).
- We schedule a 45-min technical sizing call with your Ops Eng (cc’d) and our infra lead (Ben) to walk through routing and failover.
- Based on those inputs we’ll produce two options: Hosted with geo-routing + cache and a Dedicated pool with reserved capacity.

If that sounds good I’ll loop Ben for the tech sizing and Laura for procurement/contract timeline.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
D: +1 415-555-0124 | diego_fernandez@redwood.com
[Attachment: healthsync_slo_requirements.xlsx (excel)]

From: Sara Patel <sara@healthsync.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: HealthSync Ops <ops@healthsync.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:38:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo: quick SLO follow-up and data residency check

Diego —

Thanks for the clear recap. I filled the attached sheet with conservative numbers and added notes where we need guidance (see column comments). Highlights:
- Region split: US 65% traffic, EU 25%, APAC 10% (peak distribution).
- Peak RPS (global): 800 RPS; US peak 520 RPS, EU peak 200 RPS, APAC peak 80 RPS.
- Streaming concurrency: estimate 160 concurrent streams at US peak, EU 60, APAC 20.
- Cold-start sensitivity: our product expects <300 ms first-token in US for interactive editor flows; batch exports can tolerate higher.
- Data residency: EU tenants and logs must remain in EU; backups can replicate to US for DR but must be encrypted and access-controlled.

We’ve attached the sheet and a short compliance checklist. We’re happy to do a tech sizing call Thurs or Fri morning (ET).

Sara
Sara Patel
Head of Product Ops | HealthSync
sara@healthsync.com | +1 212-555-7642
[Attachment: healthsync_slo_requirements_filled.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara@healthsync.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: quick SLO follow-up and data residency check

Hi Sara — thanks for the numbers, that helps a lot. A few quick notes from the infra sizing perspective:

- With the distribution you provided (US-heavy) we can meet p95 <= 150 ms in US with a hosted model using regional routing + prefix KV caching, assuming average sequence lengths you gave. We’ll size continuous batching windows to balance latency vs cost.
- For EU data residency: we’ll provision EU-only caches and storage paths; logs can be streamed to a customer-managed S3 in EU.
- Streaming concurrency at 160 streams is reasonable for our Dedicated pools; for Hosted we recommend a reserved concurrency reservation (burstable) to guarantee availability during your daily spikes.
- Cold-start: we can apply hot-slab pinning for your interactive editor flows (keeps model shards warm) to meet <300ms first-token for US. There’s a tradeoff in cost — I can quantify in the proposal.

I’ve attached a working latency matrix (redwood-regional-latency-matrix.pdf) with rough kernel-level latencies and expected p95 ranges for different model sizes.

Next step from our side: if you confirm Thurs 13 May 10:30am ET for the tech call we’ll invite our infra lead and provide a short runbook template to collect trace samples and a small test-set of typical prompts to run a short qualification.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
[Attachment: redwood-regional-latency-matrix.pdf (pdf)]

Sara —

Perfect — thanks for filling the sheet and the checklist. Confirming next steps (action owners and dates):

2) HealthSync to provide a 1-hour sample trace + 50 sample prompts (by EOD Thu 13 May) so we can run an initial qualification against our staging endpoints.
3) Redwood to produce a short comparison: Hosted (geo-routing + cache) vs Dedicated (reserved pool + pinning) including estimated monthly unit cost and expected p95 ranges per region (deliver by Tue, 18 May).
4) Procurement touchpoint: Laura to provide a standard SOW and procurement checklist after sizing call (Laura, pls confirm timing).

Ben — please schedule the call and include the runbook link. Laura — I’ll introduce you to Sara in a separate thread for procurement questions if that works.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.
